correctness.rationale: For the final repaired claim, K=diag(1/n) and f_n=g_n=n e_n are valid H vectors and each lies in R(K*); Kf_n=e_n so every image weave is Parseval and dominates ||K*h||^2; at x_N=e_N/N the original weaving energy is 1 and ||x_N||^2=1/N^2, giving an unbounded N^2 ratio. The range of K is dense nonclosed since (1/n) lies in its closure but has preimage (1,1,...) outside l2. For closed-range K, M=R(K*) is Hilbert and P_M f_i belong to M. Restricted energies equal those of the ambient families. For x=K* h, an ordinary M-frame gives image K-frame bounds A,B||K||^2. Conversely set h=(K*)^dagger x with ||h||<=||Kdagger|| ||x||; the image frame bounds C,D give M-frame bounds C,D||Kdagger||^2 for the projected vectors. K=0 is treated separately with arbitrary positive bounds. The finite-dimensional P_span(e1) example shows that bare closed range cannot imply literal subspace membership of unprojected f_i. The final RESULT.md supplies complete proof of all these implications; finite exact-rational experiments corroborate sample identities but do not prove the infinite result.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original substantive correction of a specific published characterization: the explicit nonclosed-range diagonal counterexample invalidates the printed reverse implication. The complete repaired final claim also explicitly separates inherited-norm coefficient inequalities from genuine subspace-frame membership, replacing the unqualified closed-range equivalence by one involving orthogonal projections onto R(K*). The 2019 source supplies a related closed-range operator lemma and Proposition 2.6, but its inspected statements do not prove the particular diagonal counterexample or this projection-aware correction. Related 2021/2024 transfer results use closed-range assumptions in different implications, not a demonstrated prior correction of this exact proposition. The full 2021 Xiang paper with DOI 10.1080/01630563.2021.1882488 was not accessible; this is a named residual literature risk, not an invented noncoverage finding.

value.rationale: The result repairs a printed necessary-and-sufficient characterization (Proposition 2.5) rather than a detached routine calculation. A nonclosed-range example destroys the entire Bessel upper bound while every image weave is an orthonormal basis. The corrected projected-family equivalence identifies two independently necessary distinctions: uniform preimage control for the coefficient inequalities and membership of original vectors in the closed operator range for literal Hilbert-space frames. It provides explicit quantitative constants and a one-index boundary witness, useful for citations/applications of the published proposition. The argument is elementary functional analysis but mathematical motivation is the substantive published gap.
